questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city to which i was travelling to and how well renowned the university was academically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think Monash did a great job in general. However, there were some minor things that took a little more time to find. However, the team that assisted us were always readily available to help with any issues we encountered.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received assistance with us arriving late, where they provided a later orientation presentation. We also received plenty of assistance with being enrolled in courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. We just looked through airbnb and found an apartment in Southbank, which was perfect for our needs. However, it needs to be noted that this is approach is definitely easier if you are travelling with someone as better offer are to be found through airbnb this way. I would definitely not recommend staying on campus, as these are far away from the city, and also because the campusesses for Monash do not have much to offer that is not academically related.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find some like minded individuals and be out in good time to find the perfect accommodation for you (preferably somewhere in central Melbourne).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are some short courses you have to do (some of them quite meaningless). Other than that just a little bit of classic enrolment work, filling out forms and such, but nothing too demanding.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a dedicated team at Monash that handle all students from abroad. These guys ar really good at helping with everything from visa requirements to enrolling in courses when you get there.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Super succesful. Monash has a very wide range of courses, so there should be lots of courses that fit and also some that you can get merits for back home.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing much, just follow the guidance, especially around the student visa application.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The BA courses were especially easy compared to back home. Lots of points are given throughout the semester, so if you are on top of your schoolwork, then you need not worry about not passing.

The MA course was a bit harder, but still very manageable compared to back home. Points were also given throughout the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Smaller class sizes so more time with the professor and more intimate in a sense. 

The style of teaching is in my opinion designed to help everyone pass, but in doing so neglects really teaching the subject to the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECC2610	Game theory and strategic thinking
ECC3690	International economics
ECF5421	Applied macroeconomics
ECX2144	The economic history of the modern world

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: We got merits transferred for mandatory courses for Economics, so would definitely recommend all of the courses above.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The visa is definitely the biggest one as it has been bumped up as well in recent times from an already extreme level. So be on the lookout for that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is definitely less expensive than back home, so is eating out. So expect your food bills - especially if you like meat - to be lower.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I cannot say as i did not indulge in any of these

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know as i did not pursue any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely just living and being in Melbourne as it is an incredible city to experience and live in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take some road trips down south to the Great Ocean Road or Phillip Island. Or take some up north to the mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Incoming students need to be aware that there are a lot of international students, especially ones from Asia. So the culture one campus is very much thereafter.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open. People in class are usually very nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some international students do not speak english very well, if at all. So beware of any group projects as this might become a challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aussies are always fun to be around :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live in the city, not on campus.
Experience the city and all the incredible culinary spots it offers.
Take road trips as Victory/southern NSW is very underrated in terms of its nature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: DO NOT live on campus!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Melbourne.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Did not really have any great challenges along the way to be fair.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
